routeGeometry.routeDescription: From Aigertstugan, the route follows the stream uphill toward Lill-Aigert with views toward Tjulträsket. It continues over open low mountain terrain and rocky/blocky high ground around Juovvatjåhkka/Juovatvaretje, where a rest shelter provides weather refuge. It descends steeply to a plateau, climbs again toward Vuomatjåhkka/Matsen rest shelter, and finally descends through mountain birch forest and marshy ground toward Servvejuhkka, its waterfall/pool side path and STF Serve.

campingAndFire.summary: There are no mapped official campsite POIs on the high section. Tenting is reported near Aigert, on sheltered outcrops/slopes, and west of Serve/by Servvejuhkka, but exposed high plateau camping can be windy, rocky and water-limited. No current fire ban was found on 2026-04-30, but fire status is live.

records.details: Reports mention tenting near fresh water at Aigert and exposed but good camping about 1 km before Aigert in reverse direction when breezy.
Field reports mention outcropping below high point, but high plateau is often too exposed/rocky or water-limited.

records.details: Juovatvaretje/Juovvatjåhkka and Vuomatjåhkka/Matsen are rest/emergency shelters, not normal overnight huts. Overnight only for emergency/fjällsäkerhet.

Sorsele fire-ban layer reported no fire ban on 2026-04-30, but fire status is live/date-sensitive. Shelter stove/wood use should be treated as facility attributes, not standalone public fireplace POIs.

rulesAndSafety.summary: No official hiking closure was found on 2026-04-30. Aigert-Serve should carry strong weather/exposure/visibility, high-top water, protected-area, dog/reindeer, winter marking, fire/weather live-check, hut-service and hunting/fishing caveats.

records.details: Länsstyrelsen current notices did not list Aigert, Serve, Servestugan, Aigertstugan, Ammarnäs or Tjulträsk as closed/rerouted. The 2026-04-16 notice says winter route poles are being removed early due snow conditions, while routes remain open and users must assess local conditions. The 2026-04-24 Juktån/Rasteselet bridge notice is off-section.

Section is within Vindelfjällen nature reserve/Natura 2000 context. Standing rules prohibit disturbing wildlife or reindeer husbandry, damaging natural features and motorized travel outside allowed roads/trails/areas.
Marsivagge bird-protection entry ban is 15 May-1 Aug and was not active on 2026-04-30. Route overlay was not resolved in this section pass.

Naturkartan/Länsstyrelsen describes the section as demanding in both summer and winter, one of Kungsleden's highest parts, and advises waiting for good weather. Field reports confirm fog around Lill-Aigert can hide markers. SMHI point forecast at check time had no warning polygon intersecting Aigert or Serve, but Serve forecast included visibility minimum 0.3 km and gusts up to 17.5 m/s.
Live Länsstyrelsen fire-ban layer for Sorsele reported no fire ban on 2026-04-30. This is a live status, not static metadata.

Current 2026-03-30 notice updated 2026-03-31 16:47 covers ongoing reindeer movement/grazing around Ammarnäs-Björkfjället-Skeble and tells local snowmobile-dispensation users to choose another route. This is not a hiking closure.
National dog-control period 1 Mar-20 Aug was active on 2026-04-30. Practical implication is leash/very close control. Reindeer calving in Vindelfjällen occurs in May.

STF Aigert and STF Serve both list 2026 opening periods 27 Feb-3 May and 18 Jun-20 Sep. Both were in service on 2026-04-30, but full-service gap begins after 2026-05-03 until 2026-06-18. Aigert has a year-round safety room; Serve has no mobile coverage.

Small-game hunting runs 25 Aug-15 Sep for Sweden residents and 16 Sep-15 Mar for all with permit; not active on 2026-04-30. Fishing requires permit; stream fishing prohibited 15 Sep-15 Oct. Activity rules only.

conditionReports.summary: Hard 19 km stage, sustained climb from Aigert, rocky high ground near Lilla Aigert, no flowing water on tops, Juovvatjåhkka emergency cabin, muddy/scrubby ground, Vuomatjåhkka shelter visible/off-trail, Servvejuhka bridge and worn tent sites before bridge.

SOBO from Serve to Aigert: Vuomatjåhkka slightly off trail, Juovvatjåhkka shelter useful in drizzle, crowded shelter, rocky lakes section, 1.5-hour shower, muddy trail, streams across path, flooded boardwalks and Serve drying room/stove useful after wind/rain.

conditionReports.reportDate: published about 2019; field date not explicit
conditionReports.summary: Reverse Serve-Aigert: hot/sunny start, two cozy rest shelters, steep climb to second shelter, strong cold wind at height, storm near Aigert, tenting near fresh water at Aigert and likely midge/gnat issue.

Reverse Serve-Aigert: cold damp camp, heavy midges low down, dry section before Juovvatjåhkka with other hikers asking for water, storms/thunder around high point, simple A-frame emergency shelter, rough block terrain and exposed but good camping about 1 km before Aigert when breezy.

Reverse Servvejávrrie-Aigertstugan: wet/windy night, slippery stones, Servvejuhka bridge by waterfall, sparse/dead birch forest, Vuomatjåhkka shelter lunch, junction toward Norra Fjällnäs, steep climb to Juovvatjåhkka, high rocky walking and long curve around large bog before Aigert.
Leaving Aigert in high wind/rain, fog at Lill-Aigert thick enough that markers were not visible; hiker stopped at Juovatvaretje rest cabin instead of continuing.

AllTrails labels route hard/strenuous around 12.1 mi; Wikiloc reverse track July 2022 reports 12.66 mi, 5h12 moving / 7h59 total; Gaia aggregates 11.7 mi and difficult. Useful for distance/difficulty corroboration, not primary conditions.
